messages.subject: Change point model
parts:
Hi users' stan,

I wrote a change point model for my design data as described in the file attached. 

However, after reading the manuel, on page 79 and 203, I'm not sur if the relation between
is correct.

In fact, for y ~Normal(0,1)T[ ,2.5] , the code of model is first y ~ Normal(0,1) then condition of constraint.

In my code on my data in file attached, I wrote log-probability in transformed parameters
and only constraint  without  the sampling of log_y. The code is bellow :

Could you tell me if is correct to do this, please ?

data { 
  int<lower=1> I; // Number of items
  int<lower=1> S; // Number of subjects
  int<lower=1> N; // Number of log-response time observed
  real<lower=0> log_L; // Lower bound log-response time observed
  real<lower=0> log_U; // Upper bound log-response time observed
  vector<lower=log_L,upper=log_U>[N] log_y; // Log-response time
}

transformed data {
  vector[S] log_unif; //  DiscreteUniform(cpp|1,I)
  
  for(s in 1:S){
    log_unif[s] = -log(I);
  }
}

parameters {
  matrix<lower=0>[S,2] mu; // Mean of each group for each subjects
  vector<lower=0>[S] sigma; // Sd of each group for each subjects
}

transformed parameters {
  vector[N] lp_new; // Log-probability of each subeject
  
  for(s in 1:S){
    vector[I] new_y; // Identification of log-response time of each subject
    vector[I] lp; 
    
    new_y = segment(log_y, (I*(s-1)+1), I);
    lp = rep_vector(log_unif[s], I);
    
    for(i in 1:I){
      for(j in 1:I){
        if(j < i) {
          lp[i] = lp[i] + normal_lpdf(new_y[j] | mu[s,1] , sigma[s]) -
          log_diff_exp(normal_lcdf(log_U | mu[s,1], sigma[s]), normal_lcdf(log_L | mu[s,1], sigma[s]));
        }
        else{
          lp[i] = lp[i] + normal_lpdf(new_y[j] | mu[s,2] , sigma[s]) -
          log_diff_exp(normal_lcdf(log_U | mu[s,2], sigma[s]), normal_lcdf(log_L | mu[s,2], sigma[s]));
        }
      }
    }
    lp_new[(I*(s-1)+1):(s*I)] = lp; 
  }
}

model { 
  to_vector(mu) ~ normal(0,5); // A priori of mean
  sigma ~ cauchy(0,1); // A priori of sd
  
  for(s in 1:S){
    for(i in (I*(s-1)+1):(s*I)){
      if (log_y[i] < log_L || log_y[i] > log_U){
        target += negative_infinity();
      }
      else{
        target += log_sum_exp(segment(lp_new, (I*(s-1)+1), I)); // Likelihood
      }
    }
  }
}

generated quantities {
  int<lower=1, upper=I> cpp[S]; // change point position
  
  for(s in 1:S){
    cpp[s] = categorical_rng(softmax(segment(lp_new, (I*(s-1)+1), I))); 
  }
}


Sorry for my English.

Bests Eric.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Change point model
parts:
I don't think the use of log_L and log_U here make sense.
Why are you truncating to exactly your observation times?

Also not sure why mu is constrained to be positive.

I'd simplify things out of that complicated transformed params
and model block and just do everyting directly without all the
fancy indexing, then if that's working, try to make it more
efficient.

To compare true values and estimates, you need the uncertainty
in the estimates, not just a point plot.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Change point model
parts:
Hi,

Thank you for answer.

My data is response time. We have a test of 10 items with time limit of 180 seconds for all the test.

Each participant on test takes a time on each item and this time is registered in matrix PxI where P is number of participants et I numbers of items.

I don't think the use of log_L and log_U here make sense.  Why are you truncating to exactly your observation times ? Also not sure why mu is constrained to be positive. 

As each time of each item is inferior to time limit 180 seconds. Then each time is between 1 and 180 seconds. As I decided to transformed response time with logarithm function. I constrained log-response between log_L = 0 and log_U = log(180). So mu for each log-response time are positif.

I'd simplify things out of that complicated transformed params 
and model block and just do everyting directly without all the 
fancy indexing, then if that's working, try to make it more 
efficient.

In the manuel, It says it is efficient to work with vector than matrix. So I transformed matrix log-response time PxI to vector log_y with length is N = PxI.
So the different indexing is to capture different response time for each subject. However, should I work with matrix ?
To compare true values and estimates, you need the uncertainty in the estimates, not just a point plot.

Is it meaning to see if true value is in 95% confidence interval ?

Best regards.

> In the manuel, It says it is efficient to work with vector than matrix. So I transformed matrix log-response time PxI to vector log_y with length is N = PxI.
> So the different indexing is to capture different response time for each subject. However, should I work with matrix ?

It says it depends on what you're doing with it. If you use
matrix multiply, you need a matrix. If you just want to
extract row or column vectors out of a matrix, then arrays of row
or column vectors is more efficient.

The key thing is to vectorize all the density calls.

> To compare true values and estimates, you need the uncertainty in the estimates, not just a point plot.
>
> Is it meaning to see if true value is in 95% confidence interval ?

It should be in 95% posterior interval 95% of the time, not all the time.

- Bob
